newsitem.title: CHINA: China's leaders woo Taiwan,pledge no change in HK.
newsitem.headline: China's leaders woo Taiwan,pledge no change in HK.

text.p: Jubilant at resuming sovereignty over Hong Kong, China's leaders urged authorities in rival Taiwan on Tuesday to follow that model and reunify with a stronger, increasingly prosperous motherland.

Just hours after Premier Li Peng urged Taiwan's authorities to take the device of Hong Kong's handover as their goal, President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin told the island to abandon any pretensions to independence.

"This is not only to celebrate the start of a new era for Hong Kong, it is also to celebrate a major victory in the peaceful reunification of China," Li told a reception to celebrate the recovery of Hong Kong at midnight on Monday after 156 years of British colonial domination.
"The 'one country, two systems' formula works for Hong Kong and Macau," Li said. "It can also work for Taiwan."

In a speech broadcast live on state television from a rally to celebrate the handover of Hong Kong, Jiang reminded China's 1.2 billion people -- including those in Hong Kong -- of the triumph of the Communist Party.

He tried to please both left and right in the powerful party hierarchy, paying tribute to communist China's founding fathers while promising his people, and those of capitalist Hong Kong, a prosperous future.
The "one country, two systems" formula devised by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping to recover Hong Kong without altering its freewheeling system was a model, Jiang said.
"It will set an example for...the final solution to the Taiwan question," he said, reminding rival Taiwan not to try to seek independence. Beijing sees the island as a rebel province.

"We hope that the Taiwan authorities will, setting store by the overall interests of our nation, truly return to the one-China position," Jiang told an audience of 80,000 in Beijing's Workers' Stadium.
"We hope that the Taiwan authorities will... take concrete steps towards the development of cross-Straits relations and to the complete reunification of the country," he said.
The speeches marked China's most explicit suggestion to Taiwan since the Hong Kong handover hours earlier that it should follow the territory's example.
"The prospect of complete national reunification... now stands promisingly in sight," Jiang said.

Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan said Taiwan could never accept communist rule. Reunification was possible only if China, like Taiwan, adopted multiparty democracy -- a scheme Lien dubbed "one country, one good system".

Analysts say reunification is a key policy goal for China's leadership, which sees boosting patriotic sentiment among the population as a way to bolster communist credentials eroded by nearly two decades of market-style economic reform.

On the 76th birthday of the Chinese Communist Party, Jiang told his people that their prosperity, China's stability, the return of Hong Kong and a glittering future were possible only under communist rule.

Repeating again China's commitment to respect its agreement to leave Hong Kong untouched after the handover, Jiang promised also to push forward the economic reform policies of Deng, his late mentor, but made no mention of political change.

Jiang smiled and even sang along during the rally when thousands of schoolchildren waved flags, hundreds of costumed dancers performed massive socialist-style synchronised numbers and some of Hong Kong's and China's pop superstars crooned.
The show ended with a thundering display of 1,997 fireworks to celebrate the year in which Beijing recovered Hong Kong.
"The 100-year expectation of the Chinese people has finally come true," Jiang said.
